thread:
anna_oncall: @channel :rotating_light: Seeing cross-region replication latency spike between us-west1 <-> eu-west1 since ~10:03 UTC. KV lag up to 45s, scheduler failing to bind GPUs for smaller shards. Queue depth for low-priority customers climbing. Kicking off emergency thread.

marta_infra: copying metrics: region_link_error_rate=12%, kv_replication_lag=45s, pod_pending=320, available_gpu_pools=60% of normal. p95 latency to eu-west1 from us-west1 ~ 2.1s -> 8.7s.

chris_sre: any recent infra changes? net infra alerts?

deploy-bot: Deploy 2026-03-18T09:58:21Z: rolling update finished on us-west1-control-plane (no failures).

marta_infra: no infra deploys at 09:58 besides control-plane patch which should be safe. Network vendor reported partial flap on inter-region fabric affecting large flows; small flows fine.

anna_oncall: immediate mitigation proposals: 1) apply temporary per-customer softcaps for best-effort tier; 2) failover traffic for critical customers to ap-south standby region (higher latency) via smart-routing; 3) enable model-variant fallback to quantized x4 model for latency-sensitive routes; 4) prevent new on-demand GPU allocation for non-enterprise tenants. Thoughts on ordering?

chris_sre: +1 to ordering. We should do softcaps first to relieve scheduling. Then enable model fallback for high-QPS routes.

marta_infra: I'm prepping throttle configs. Draft command to apply softcap by tier:
```
redwoodctl quota patch --scope=tenant-tier --target=best-effort --hard-limit=0.6 --note="auto softcap during cross-region fabric incident"
```
This will drop throughput for best-effort to 60% of baseline.

anna_oncall: run it against a canary first (tenant-tier=beta-customers) then roll to all best-effort. Canary window 2m.

marta_infra: executing canary now.

ops-bot: action: quota patch canary started by marta_infra for tenant-tier=beta-customers at 10:12 UTC.

marta_infra: canary metrics after 90s: queue depth reduced 18%, pod_pending reduced 12%, KV lag stable at 43s. No customer-facing 5xx spikes in canary subset.

chris_sre: good. roll to all best-effort. Also let's set per-customer emergency softcap for top noisy tenants:
```
redwoodctl throttle set --customer-id=acct-C12345 --qps=6 --reason="emergency softcap"
redwoodctl throttle set --customer-id=acct-D98765 --qps=10 --reason="emergency softcap"
```
This keeps them from monopolizing preemptible GPU slots.

marta_infra: applying global best-effort softcap now.

ops-bot: action: global softcap applied for tenant-tier=best-effort at 10:16 UTC by marta_infra.

diego_product: FYI, we should also notify a couple enterprise customers who may see degraded perf if routed to ap-south. I'll draft message if we decide to shift.

anna_oncall: do we need to trigger region failover policy for SLA customers? Decision matrix: only shift customers with explicit failover opt-in. For others, prefer model fallback + reserved capacity bump if possible.

marta_infra: reserved pool bump: can move 8 dedicated nodes from eu-west1 spare pool to SLA customers in us-west1 but that requires deprovisioning some lower-priority reserved capacity. Need approval.

chris_sre: I approve reassigning spare dedicated nodes to maintain SLAs. We'll document and reverse once fabric stable.

julia_support: prepping customer comms templates. Need list of impacted enterprise tenants who will be bumped/shifted. Please @mention when decided.

marta_infra: added model-variant fallback on routing layer for routes with latency-sensitive flag: prefer quantized-q4 variants. Command:
```
infra-router update-route --service=chat.generate --fallback-model=redwood/llama-q4 --criteria="latency>300ms OR kv_lag>30s"
```
Initial canary done for 5% of sessions.

anna_oncall: early telemetry: overall p95 token latency down from 1.4s -> 1.1s for on-fallback sessions; cost per token reduced but output quality slightly degraded for some prompts. Track quality regressions.

chris_sre: we should also throttle background batch jobs that schedule long sequences. marta, can you add a rule to deprioritize batch inference and block new batch jobs until we are within healthy kv lag?

marta_infra: adding rule: `scheduler set-priority --workload=batch --max-concurrency=2 --block-new=true`

ops-bot: batch scheduling restrictions activated at 10:24 UTC.

anna_oncall: action checklist: 
- [x] Canary softcap -> success
- [x] Global best-effort softcap applied
- [x] Per-tenant emergency throttles applied for noisy tenants
- [x] Model-variant fallback canary enabled
- [x] Batch jobs deprioritized
- [ ] Reserved node reassignment in progress (marta)
- [ ] Customer comms (julia/diego)
- [ ] Vendor network case open (marta)

marta_infra: opening vendor ticket now, priority P0.

ops-bot: vendor network ticket created: NET-7894. Vendor ETA initial triage 10m.

diego_product: customer comm drafts ready, tagging impacted SLAs list from billing sync. Will ping when reserved nodes are moved.

chris_sre: scoreboard: kv lag steady ~42-45s; pod_pending down 40% from peak; GPU allocations paused for non-enterprise. Continue monitoring 5m intervals. If kv_lag < 20s and pod_pending < 50 we can begin reversing softcaps.

anna_oncall: agreed. I'll keep this thread as the incident single source of truth. Drop updates every 5 minutes or on any change. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
